subject: SIG follow-up: log sampling, access windows, and training on customer data
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@medisys.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medisys.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: data handling clarifications needed

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the initial SIG matrix your team provided last week. Our InfoSec team has a couple of follow-up items specifically around runtime logs, sampling for analytics, and whether any customer content ever ends up in training corpora. Could you confirm: 

1) Retention windows for raw request/response logs vs. structured telemetry (per-customer defaults and enterprise carve-outs).
2) Whether KV cache / transient in-memory state is ever persisted to disk or to long-term logs.
3) Do you ever use customer data to fine-tune or train models? If so, what opt-in/opt-out controls and evidence (audits) exist?

We'd like short answers and any supporting artifacts (audit CSVs, diagrams) we can attach to our vendor risk file.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Senior Security Engineer, MediSys
security@medisys.com

Attachment: Medisys_SIG_questions_20270608.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: data handling clarifications needed

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and technical detail below.

1) Retention: default host: raw request/response logs are retained 7 days by default for hosted customers; structured telemetry (usage metrics, aggregated latency/cost) retained 365 days. Enterprise accounts may contract longer retention or shorter TTLs; we support per-account retention overrides (SLA/contract).

2) KV cache / transient state: KV caches live in GPU process memory and are ephemeral; they are not written to persistent store as part of normal runtime. We may collect aggregated KV cache hit-rate metrics (no raw content) for performance tuning. Attach: kv-cache-ephemerality-diagram.png.

3) Training on customer data: by default we do NOT use customer prompt/response pairs to train or fine-tune models. We have an opt-in program for research/aggregate improvements that is contractually explicit; opt-in must be initiated by the customer and recorded in our provisioning system. When enabled, data used for research is sampled, redacted per policy, and stored in a segregated bucket with access controls and export logs.

I'll drop a technical note from Soojin that answers the persistence and sampling artifacts. Attached is a one-page SIG answer packet and an access-audit sample CSV for an example enterprise account.

Next steps: if MediSys wants a formal attestation, we can provide a signed letter and a SCIF of the audit CSVs.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270614_REDWOOD_SIG_answers_v1.pdf, access-audit-sample.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: data handling clarifications needed

Hi Aisha —

Adding the technical specifics you asked for:

- Raw logs vs telemetry: raw request/response logs (full payloads) go to a short-lived partition and are retained for 7 days by default on hosted customers. These logs are truncated sooner if a customer requests an ephemeral profile in their account settings (we support 24h or 0d TTLs for sensitive workloads). Aggregated telemetry (token counts, latencies, error rates) are rolled up and stored for 365 days for observability.

- KV cache: the runtime uses an in-memory KV cache (GPU DRAM / host RAM) to keep model key/value state between tokens. This state is never serialized to long-term storage under normal operation. During crash-dump debugging or customer-requested memory snapshots (rare, incident response), we may persist a memory snapshot to a secured bucket — that flow requires an access request, approvals (on-call + security), and is logged in our incident audit trail. We have an automated process to zero out keys post-capture. Evidence: see attached kv-cache-ephemerality-diagram.png and the sample audit rows in access-audit-sample.csv.

- Training/fine-tuning: Redwood's policy is explicit: we DO NOT train on customer prompt/response pairs unless the customer has a documented, signed opt-in. Opt-in flow: (1) customer signs a data-use addendum or explicit consent via procurement; (2) the customer environment flag is set; (3) data selected for research is redacted using our PII pipeline and a review queue; (4) exports are stored in a segregated research bucket with MFA and narrow IAM roles; (5) all accesses are logged and audited quarterly. We maintain an internal table of opt-in enrollments and can export it for audit.

- Sampling for analytics: we sample requests at configurable rates for product analytics (default 1 in 1000 for payloads, 1 in 100 for metadata). Samples are hashed (non-reversible) against customer IDs to produce aggregated metrics; raw payload samples are only kept if account has opt-in for research or debugging, otherwise they are discarded after TTL.

- Evidence and audits: we can provide CSVs showing access events for the last 90 days, the opt-in audit table, and our SOC2 report redactions. We also maintain a SIG artifact pack.

If you want, I can produce a small checklist that maps each SIG question to the evidence artifact filename.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Principal Systems Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-cache-ephemerality-diagram.png
